entries.title: Cubs' Nico Hoerner likely day-to-day after leaving win over Diamondbacks with 'left-sided neck tightness'
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> survived a couple of big scares Friday in a 6-5 victory over the Diamondbacks at Wrigley Field, their third straight win.</p><p>Second baseman Nico Hoerner exited abruptly in the second inning with what the team called “left-sided neck tightness.” But it looks like Hoerner, off to an All-Star-caliber start, might be only day-to-day.</p><p>The two-time Gold Glover didn’t even rule out returning Saturday.</p><p>“It’s probably something a lot of people out there have dealt with, where your neck just kind of gets stuck,” Hoerner said after the Cubs won for the 13th time in 16 games. “It had locked up moving around pregame and then just wasn’t in a good place on the field.</p><p>“So got some good treatment and see where we’re at tomorrow. Not an injury, but the kind of thing that didn’t leave me in a place to be myself today.”</p><p>Hoerner is batting .297 with four homers and team-best 26 RBIs through 32 games. He’s been slick, sometimes sensational, in the field again this season.</p><p>Facing D-Backs starter Zac Gallen, Hoerner led off the bottom of the first with a liner to the left-center gap for his team-leading ninth double. Video showed Hoerner gritted his teeth after he rounded first.</p><p>He remained on the bases, then came around and scored on Michael Busch’s two-out, two-run single in the Cubs’ three-run rally.</p><p>Hoerner was in the field for the top of the second but got no action. Utility man Matt Shaw pinch-hit for Hoerner in the bottom of the inning, then replaced him in the field for the third.</p><p>The Cubs signed Hoerner, to a $141 million, six contract in March, cementing the 28-year-old as one of their cornerstone players — one they could ill afford to lose along with nine pitchers who have gone down with injuries since the start of spring training.</p><p>That leads us to the second scare on Friday. The Cubs narrowly escaped a near meltdown right after starter Colin Rea exited after 102 pitches and held on.</p><p>After the North Siders opened a 6-1 lead in the fourth, Arizona charged back behind a four-hit day by second-baseman Ildemaro Vargas and a four-run sixth inning keyed by Geraldo Perdomo’s three-run homer off reliever Ryan Rolison.</p><p>First the good news. </p><p>Rea exited with one out in the sixth and 102 pitches, again filling a spot in the rotation with Cade Horton out for the season after his second Tommy John surgery and Justin Steele taking longer than hoped to return from his second reconstructive elbow procedure.</p><p>Rea allowed two runs on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings, but was consistently over the plate as he struck out six and walked none in improving to 4-1.</p><p>“That was the biggest thing, just getting ahead of this team, trying to put them in a hole early” said the big right-hander. “I felt like we did a good job of that. They also, you know had some long at-bats to drive the pitch count up.”</p><p>Rea left with one out and an Arizona runner on first in the sixth. </p><p>The D-backs rallied in a hurry agains reliever Rolison, making his fourth appearance with the Cubs since they picked him up off waivers from the White Sox in January. Rolison entered having allowed no runs on three hits in six previous innings with the North Siders. He had walked none.</p><p>The first four Arizona batters against Rolison reached base. Pinch-hitter Tim Tawa walked. Jorge Barrosa doubled on a bunt that rolled past third baseman Alex Bregman, hit the bag, created confusion and allowed a run to score.</p><p>Geraldo Perdomo followed with a three-run homer to left on a 2-0 fastball that cut it to 6-5.  For good measure, Vargas then lined a single to left, his fourth on the day as he extended his hitting streak to 27 games.</p><p>Rolison regrouped to strike out Corbin Carroll and Adrian Del Castillo to retire the side. The left-hander was charged with three runs as his ERA went from 0.00 to 4.05</p><p>Phil Maton tossed a 1-2-3 seventh. Jacob Webb pitched the final two hitless innings, striking out three and walking one for his first save with the Cubs and eighth his seven-year career. </p><p>“He pitched great,” manager Craig Counsell said. “Getting six outs at the end of the game is very difficult." </p><p>The Cubs looked like they might coast in this one.</p><p>Busch had two more hits has he inched his average up to .203 following an icy start at the plate.</p><p>His single made it 2-0 in the first. Ian Happ came home to make it 3-0 when Carson Kelly’s routine pop fell between center fielder and Mount Carmel product Alek Thomas, and second baseman Vargas for a single and first of Kelly’s two hits.</p><p>Vargas' second single drove in a run to cut to 3-1 in the fourth.</p><p>The Cubs jumped out 6-1 in the bottom half, scoring on a Dansby Swanson RBI single, a wild pitch and Bregman’s entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — Outfielder Jarred Kelenic is back where he wants to be: in the major leagues with the White Sox.</p><p>He wasn’t in their starting lineup Friday against the Padres at Petco Park, but he wasn’t at Triple-A Charlotte, either.</p><p>The Sox and Kelenic, whom the Mets selected with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2018 draft, had high hopes in spring training. But he didn’t make the team.</p><p>‘‘I think the message was pretty clear,’’ Kelenic, 26, said before the game. ‘‘Really focus on controlling the strike zone. They were really high on my talent. They knew that as long as I began controlling the strike zone and getting my ‘A’ swing out, good things would happen.’’</p><p>The adjustments he made apparently were good enough. Kelenic was called up when the Sox put Everson Pereira on the injured list Wednesday with a strained muscle on the right side of his chest.</p><p>It wasn’t as though Kelenic was lighting up the minor leagues. In 26 games, he hit .202 with six home runs, 18 RBI, 16 runs scored and seven stolen bases.</p><p>But the bulk of those numbers came in his last 10 games, when he hit .333 (12-for-36) with five homers, 12 RBI and 10 runs scored.</p><p>Kelenic pinch-hit in the ninth inning of the Sox’ 3-2, 10-inning victory Wednesday against the Angels at Rate Field and struck out swinging. He batted .179 in spring training before the Sox demoted him. They’re hoping for the best now.</p><p>‘‘It was a tough decision to send him down,’’ manager Will Venable said about Kelenic, who was in camp as non-roster invitee. ‘‘He hadn’t really tapped into his best swing. He did some good things defensively. He clicked on a couple of balls at the plate in camp. But he wasn’t the best version of himself.</p><p>‘‘He went down, struggled a little bit early but did some quality work to get himself back on track to be the best version of himself. And that’s what we expect to get out of him now.’’</p><p>Despite being drafted by the Mets, Kelenic never played for them. He was traded to the Mariners on Dec. 3, 2018, in the deal that sent second baseman Robinson Cano and closer Edwin Diaz to the Mets.</p><p>Things, however, didn’t develop well for Kelenic. The Mariners were excited to get him, but he batted a combined .168 with 167 strikeouts in 147 games in 2021 and 2022.</p><p>He had played so poorly that in mid-2023 he fractured his left foot kicking a Gatorade cooler in the home dugout out of frustration. It was then on to the Braves, but it didn’t work out for him with them, either.</p><p>The Sox might be his final stand.</p><p>‘‘The game is hard,’’ Kelenic told the Sun-Times during spring training. ‘‘The game sucks sometimes, man. It’ll beat you down. But at the end of the day, you’ve just got to stick to your strengths and superpowers. Ride with those and have as much confidence as you can in yourself in a game where you’re set up to fail.’’</p><p>If he fails again, the time might be coming for a career change. He was one of the highest-drafted players ever from Wisconsin, despite never playing for Waukesha West High School, and turned down a scholarship offer to play college ball at Louisville after he was drafted by the Mets.</p><p>It has been a downhill slog ever since, and it was just another blow when the Sox told Kelenic this spring that he hadn’t made the team. It was Charlotte or bust.</p><p>‘‘I think something like that would be disappointing for anybody,’’ he said Friday. ‘‘But it’s baseball. It’s the industry. The only option to make the team was to go down and focus on my own game, focus on what makes me great.’’<br></p>

entries.title: Cubs closer Daniel Palencia nearing return, but might not return as closer immediately
entries.summary: <p>Closer <b>Daniel Palencia</b> is nearing a return, but the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> might not rush him back into his high-leverage role.</p><p>Palencia, who went on the injured list with a strained left oblique April 14, pitched two-thirds of an inning Friday night and allowed a hit and struck out a batter for Triple-A Iowa against St. Paul in Minnesota.</p><p>He threw 19 pitches, 14 for strikes.</p><p>It might be a one-appearance tune-up for Palencia, who last took the mound for the Cubs on April 12 against the Pirates and earned a win by tossing a scoreless ninth as the Cubs rallied.</p><p>“Optimistic we can get him back here after that outing, if all things go well,” manager <b>Craig Counsell </b>said before the Cubs’ 6-5 victory over the Diamondbacks at Wrigley Field.</p><p>Asked if Palencia will return immediately as the closer, Counsell said, “He’ll go back to getting outs. We’ve got to get Danny pitching. We want to get him pitching a lot. He’s got five innings right now.”</p><p>Palencia, 26, who had 22 saves in a breakout 2025, made five appearance this season — each one inning — before getting hurt. He’s 1-0 with one save and hasn’t allowed a run in 2026. Palencia has struck out five, walked two and allowed three hits.</p><p>Lefty reliever <b>Caleb Thielbar</b> and righty <b>Hunter Harvey</b> have been throwing and progressing toward a return as the Cubs’ staff inches back after losing nine pitchers since the start of spring training.</p><p>Thielbar, who went out with a strained left hamstring last week, might be close to returning. Harvey, sidelined since April 9 with right triceps inflammation, is further off, Counsell said.</p><h3>Pain everywhere</h3><p>The Cubs have lost pitchers to all types of injuries — not just damaged arms — and that’s what has team president <b>Jed Hoyer’s </b>head spinning as much as the sheer number of casualties.</p><p>“We’ve had knees and back and lats and elbow and shoulders, so it’s not like we’ve had just consistently one injury or another,” Hoyer said to reporters before the game. “I think there’s some randomness in there, as well.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/05/01/cubs-nico-hoerner-exits-game-with-left-sided-neck-tightness-per-team" >Cubs’ Nico Hoerner likely day-to-day after leaving win over Diamondbacks with ‘left-sided neck tightness’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>The Cubs’ staff figures to solidify as many of the injured pitchers return, even if starter <b>Cade Horton </b>and reliever <b>Porter Hodge</b> are lost for the season after Tommy John surgery.</p><p>“We obviously need to get healthy, and some of the guys we counted on to come up need to get healthy,’’ Hoyer said.</p><p>‘‘I’m sure it’s going to be a summer of working through our internal guys, but external is going to be a real thing as we go on.”</p><p>He said the team has been trying to acquire arms via trade and has been “looking really consistently for small transactions.”</p><p>Anything major might not happen until later in the season.</p><p>“It’s also May 1, and it takes awhile for those things to happen,” Hoyer said. “We’re going to have to wait and handle those things internally.”</p><h3>Steele setback no surprise</h3><p>Hoyer said he wasn’t surprised lefty starter <b>Justin Steele’s</b> return from Tommy John surgery was pushed back until after the All-Star break. Originally, the Cubs hoped Steele, their All-Star ace at 16-5 with a 3.06 ERA in a breakout 2023, might be back no later than June.</p><p>But more than a year after Steele, 30, underwent a second major surgery on his left elbow, new imaging done Tuesday showed a flexor strain that will delay his comeback, Counsell said.</p><p>“I don’t think it’s something unexpected,” Hoyer said. “Candidly, for everything to go perfectly, it was going to be a 60-day injured list, and late May, early June would have been, like, perfection. I don’t think we expect those things with second Tommy John and flexor-surgery rehabs.”</p><div class="PageListC" data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Mets plan to keep Carlos Mendoza as manager despite 10-21 start
entries.summary: <p>ANAHEIM, Calif. — Despite a 10-21 start and a recent 12-game losing streak, the New York Mets are expected to keep Carlos Mendoza as manager, according to president of baseball operations David Stearns.</p><p>The Mets snapped their franchise-worst 12-game losing streak on April 22 with a 3-2 win over the Minnesota Twins. They've since lost five of the last six, including getting swept by the Rockies. New York's 10-21 record is the worst in baseball.</p><p>"We know our record is not what we want, and we know we are capable of more," Stearns told MLB.com on Friday. "We don't view this as a manager problem, and we don't intend to make a change."</p><p>Mendoza confirmed the conversation with Stearns before Friday's opener of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels.</p><p>"I talked to David this morning," Mendoza said. "We got on the phone and we talked, and yes, that's about it. Obviously, I'm not going to get into the details of the conversation, but it was this morning that I spoke with him."</p><p>The Mets are last in the National League East, two games behind the Philadelphia Phillies, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/mlb/2026/04/28/phillies-fire-manager-rob-thomson-after-disappointing-start" >parted ways with manager Rob Thomson</a> on Tuesday morning. The Phillies have since won three straight under interim manager Don Mattingly.</p><p>"I understand the situation. We all understand the situation," Mendoza said. "It's good to have that conversation with (Stearns), but at the end of the day, we have a job and we have a responsibility. Since Day 1, since I've been in this job, I feel the support from (owners) Steve and Alex (Cohen), and David. I love working for them.</p><p>"We have a really good working relationship here. But it's about the results on the field as well. Steve is not happy. Alex is not happy. David is not happy. I'm not happy. All of us are frustrated."</p><p>Mendoza was hired in 2023 and is on the last guaranteed year of a three-year contract. He has led New York to a 182-173 overall record.</p><p>"Together, we've got to find a way to get these guys out of, out of this funk, and that we will continue to do," Mendoza said. "I'm pretty confident in our coaches, our players, that this will turn."</p><p>The Mets collapsed in 2025, going from the baseball's best record in June to barely finishing above .500, ending second in the NL East at 83–79 and missing the playoffs.<br></p>
